perimysial: (a) Surrounding a muscle or muscles. (b) Of or pertaining to the perimysium.
perceptivity: The quality or state of being perceptive; power of perception. Locke.
peperino: A volcanic rock, formed by the cementing together of sand, scoria, cinders, etc.
persisting: Inclined to persist; tenacious of purpose; persistent. -- Per*sist"ing*ly, adv.
peregrine: Foreign; not native; extrinsic or from without; exotic. [Spelt also pelegrine.] "Peregrine and preternatural heat." Bacon. Peregrine falcon (Zoöl.), a courageous and swift falcon (Falco peregrinus), remarkable for its wide distribution over all the continents.
peacock: 1. (Zoöl.) The male of any pheasant of the genus Pavo, of which at least two species are known, native of Southern Asia and the East Indies. Note: The upper tail coverts, which are long and capable of erection, are each marked with a black spot bordered by concentric bands of brilliant blue, green, and golden colors. The common domesticated species is Pavo cristatus.
pelota: A Basque, Spanish, and Spanish-American game played in a court, in which a ball is struck with a wickerwork racket.
pebbly: Full of pebbles; pebbled. "A hard, pebbly bottom." Johnson.
pequots: A tribe of Indians who formerly inhabited Eastern Connecticut. [Written also Pequods.]
pendice: A sloping roof; a lean-to; a penthouse. (old) Fairfax.
perineurial: Surrounding nerves or nerve fibers; of or pertaining to the perineurium.
pendicle: An appendage; something dependent on another; an appurtenance; a pendant. Sir W. Scott.
perennibranchiata: Those Batrachia which retain their gills through life, as the menobranchus.
pensionary: 1. Maintained by a pension; receiving a pension; as, pensionary spies. Donne. 2. Consisting of a pension; as, a pensionary provision for maintenance. | 1. One who receives a pension; a pensioner. E. Hall. 2. One of the chief magistrates of towns in Holland. Grand pensionary, the title of the prime minister, or or president of the Council, of Holland…
pellet: 1. A little ball; as, a pellet of wax . 2. A bullet; a ball for firearms. (old) Bacon. As swift as a pellet out of a gun. Chaucer. Pellet molding (Arch.), a narrow band ornamented with smalt, flat… | To form into small balls. (old) Shak.
perversion: The act of perverting, or the state of being perverted; a turning from truth or right; a diverting from the true intent or object; a change to something worse; a turning or applying to a wrong end or use. "Violations and perversions of the laws." Bacon.
periphrastic: Expressing, or expressed, in more words than are necessary; characterized by periphrase; circumlocutory. Periphrastic conjugation (Gram.), a conjugation formed by the use of the simple verb with one or more auxiliaries.
pettifog: To do a petty business as a lawyer; also, to do law business in a petty or tricky way. "He takes no money, but pettifogs gratis." S. Butler. | To advocate like a pettifogger; to argue trickily; as, to pettifog a claim. [Colloq.]
personage: 1. Form, appearance, or belongings of a person; the external appearance, stature, figure, air, and the like, of a person. "In personage stately." Hayward. The damsel well did view his personage. Spenser. 2. Character assumed or represented. "The actors and personages of this fable." Broome. "Disguised in a false personage." Addison. 3. A notable or distinguished person;
penologist: One versed in, or a student of, penology.
pectineal: (a) Of or pertaining to the pecten. (b) Relating to, or connected with, the pubic bone.
penumbrala: Of or pertaining to a penumbra; resembling a penumbra; partially illuminated.
pedomotive: Moved or worked by the action of the foot or feet on a pedal or treadle.
pearleyed: Having a pearly speck in the eye; afflicted with the cataract.
perceivance: Power of perceiving. (old) "The senses and common perceivance." Milton.
pentail: A peculiar insectivore (Ptilocercus Lowii) of Borneo; -- so called from its very long, quill-shaped tail, which is scaly at the base and plumose at the tip.
pentadactyloid: Having the form of, or a structure modified from, a pentadactyl limb.
percaline: A fine kind of French cotton goods, usually of one color.
pectin: One of a series of carbohydrates, commonly called vegetable jelly, found very widely distributed in the vegetable kingdom, especially in ripe fleshy fruits, as apples, cranberries, etc. It is extracted as variously colored, translucent substances, which are soluble in hot water but become viscous on cooling.
pedicular: Of or pertaining to lice; having the lousy distemper (phthiriasis); lousy. Southey.
permanence: The quality or state of being permanent; continuance in the same state or place; duration; fixedness; as, the permanence of institutions; the permanence of nature.
pecunious: Abounding in money; wealthy; rich. (old) Sherwood.
perilymphatic: (a) Pertaining to, or containing, perilymph. (b) Perilymphangial.
pentapetalous: Having five petals, or flower leaves.
pelargonium: A large genus of plants of the order Geraniaceæ, differing from Geranium in having a spurred calyx and an irregular corolla. Note: About one hundred and seventy species are known, nearly all of them natives of South Africa, and many having very beautiful blossoms. See the Note under Geranium.
percale: A fine cotton fabric, having a linen finish, and often printed on one side, -- used for women's and children's wear.
pedestrian: Going on foot; performed on foot; as, a pedestrian journey. | A walker; one who journeys on foot; a foot traveler; specif., a professional walker or runner.
perimysium: The connective tissue sheath which surrounds a muscle, and sends partitions inwards between the bundles of muscular fibers.
perique: A kind of tobacco with medium-sized leaf, small stem, tough and gummy fiber, raised in Louisiana, and cured in its own juices, so as to be very dark colored, usually black. It is marketed in tightly wrapped rolls called carottes.
pelasgian: 1. Of or pertaining to the Pelasgians, an ancient people of Greece, of roving habits. 2. (Zoöl.) Wandering.
perterebration: The act of boring through. (old) Ainsworth.
pellicle: 1. A thin skin or film. 2. (Chem.) A thin film formed on the surface of an evaporating solution.
peregal: Fully equal. (old) Chaucer. "Peregal to the best." Spenser.
pervasion: The act of pervading, passing, or spreading through the whole extent of a thing. Boyle.
peregrinator: One who peregrinates; one who travels about.
performable: Admitting of being performed, done, or executed; practicable.
petitionary: 1. Supplicatory; making a petition. Pardon Rome, and any petitionary countrymen. Shak. 2. Containing a petition; of the nature of a petition; as, a petitionary epistle. Swift.
petrifactive: 1. Having the quality of converting organic matter into stone; petrifying. 2. Pertaining to, or characterized by, petrifaction. The . . . petrifactive mutations of hard bodies. Sir T. Browne.
petrous: 1. Like stone; hard; stony; rocky; as, the petrous part of the temporal bone. Hooper. 2. (Anat.) Same as Petrosal.
pestilently: In a pestilent manner; mischievously; destructively. "Above all measure pestilently noisome." Dr. H. More.
pentandrous: Of or pertaining to the class Pentadria; having five stamens.
perceptible: Capable of being perceived; cognizable; discernible; perceivable. With a perceptible blast of the air. Bacon. -- Per*cep"ti*ble*ness, n. -- Per*cep"ti*bly, adv.
pebrine: An epidemic disease of the silkworm, characterized by the presence of minute vibratory corpuscles in the blood.
perpetrate: To do or perform; to carry through; to execute, commonly in a bad sense; to commit (as a crime, an offense); to be guilty of; as, to perpetrate a foul deed. What the worst perpetrate, or best endure. Young.
penetrate: 1. To enter into; to make way into the interior of; to effect an entrance into; to pierce; as, light penetrates darkness. 2. To affect profoundly through the senses or feelings; | To pass; to make way; to pierce. Also used figuratively. Preparing to penetrate to the north and west. J. R. Green. Born where Heaven's influence scarce can penetrate. Pope.
penmanship: The use of the pen in writing; the art of writing; style or manner of writing; chirography; as, good or bad penmanship.
peirameter: A dynamometer for measuring the force required to draw wheel carriages on roads of different constructions. G. Francis.
peritreme: (a) That part of the integument of an insect which surrounds the spiracles. (b) The edge of the aperture of a univalve shell.
pettitoes: The toes or feet of a pig, -- often used as food; sometimes, in contempt, the human feet. Shak.
permians: A tribe belonging to the Finnic race, and inhabiting a portion of Russia.
perispomenon: A word which has the circumflex accent on the last syllable. Goodwin.
peddling: 1. Hawking; acting as a peddler. 2. Petty; insignificant. "The miserable remains of a peddling commerce." Burke.
pelican: 1. (Zoöl.) Any large webfooted bird of the genus of Pelecanus, of which about a dozen species are known. They have an enormous bill, to the lower edge of which is attached a pouch in which captured fishes are temporarily stored. peen: (a) A round-edged, or hemispherical, end to the head of a hammer or sledge, used to stretch or bend metal by indentation. (b) The sharp-edged end of the head of a mason's hammer. | To draw, bend, or straighten, as metal, by blows with the peen of a hammer or sledge.
penetralia: 1. The recesses, or innermost parts, of any thing or place, especially of a temple or palace. 2. Hidden things or secrets; privacy; sanctuary; as, the sacred penetralia of the home.
pelicanstate: Louisiana; -- a nickname alluding to the device on its seal.
peptohydrochloric: Designating a hypothetical acid (called peptohydrochloric acid, pepsinhydrochloric acid, and chloropeptic acid) which is supposed to be formed when pepsin and dilute (0.1-0.4 per cent) hydrochloric acid are mixed together.
pernotfurnace: A reverberatory furnace with a circular revolving hearth, -- used in making steel.
perigeum: That point in the orbit of the moon which is nearest to the earth; -- opposed to Ant: apogee. It is sometimes, but rarely, used of the nearest points of other orbits, as of a comet, a planet, etc. Called also epigee, epigeum.
pegasean: Of or pertaining to Pegasus, or, figuratively, to poetry.
peristeropodous: Having pigeonlike feet; -- said of those gallinaceous birds that rest on all four toes, as the curassows and megapods.
pen: 1. A feather. (old) Spenser. 2. A wing. (old) Milton. 3. An instrument used for writing with ink, formerly made of a reed, or of the quill of a goose or other bird, but now also of other materials,… | To write; to compose and commit to paper; to indite; to compose; as, to pen a sonnet. "A prayer elaborately penned." Milton.
pentacron: A solid having five summits or angular points.
peptone: (a) The soluble and diffusible substance or substances into which albuminous portions of the food are transformed by the action of the gastric and pancreatic juices. Peptones are also formed from albuminous matter by the action of boiling water and boiling dilute acids.
petiole: 1. (Bot.) A leafstalk; the footstalk of a leaf, connecting the blade with the stem. See Illust. of Leaf. 2. (Zoöl.) A stalk or peduncle.
pentadecane: A hydrocarbon of the paraffin series, (C15H32) found in petroleum, tar oil, etc., and obtained as a colorless liquid; -- so called from the fifteen carbon atoms in the molecule.
pentamerus: A genus of extinct Paleozoic brachiopods, often very abundant in the Upper Silurian. Pentamerus limestone (Geol.), a Silurian limestone composed largely of the shells of Pentamerus.
peag: A kind of aboriginal shell money, or wampum, of the Atlantic coast of the United States; -- originally applied only to polished white cylindrical beads.
pericystitis: Inflammation of the tissues surrounding the bladder.
pendentive: (a) The portion of a vault by means of which the square space in the middle of a building is brought to an octagon or circle to receive a cupola. (b) The part of a groined vault which is supported by, and springs from, one pier or corbel.
persulphocyanic: Pertaining to, or designating, a yellow crystalline substance (called also perthiocyanic acid), analogous to sulphocyanic acid, but containing more sulphur.
periostracum: A chitinous membrane covering the exterior of many shells; -- called also epidermis.
petroglyphy: The art or operation of carving figures or inscriptions on rock or stone.
peroxidation: Act, process, or result of peroxidizing; oxidation to a peroxide.
pectoriloquial: Pertaining to, or of the nature of, pectoriloquy.
petrify: 1. To convert, as any animal or vegetable matter, into stone or stony substance. A river that petrifies any sort of wood or leaves. Kirwan. 2. To make callous or obdurate; to stupefy; to paralyze; | 1. To become stone, or of a stony hardness, as organic matter by calcareous deposits. 2. Fig.: To become stony, callous, or obdurate. Like Niobe we marble grow, And petrify with grief. Dryden.
petulant: 1. Forward; pert; insolent; wanton. (old) Burton. 2. Capriciously fretful; characterized by ill-natured freakishness; irritable. "Petulant moods." Macaulay. Syn. -- Irritable; ill-humored; peevish; cross; fretful; querulous.
periclinium: The involucre which surrounds the common receptacle in composite flowers.
pericarpial: Of or pertaining to a pericarp.
petite: Small, little; of a woman or girl, of small size and trim figure.
perissad: Odd; not even; -- said of elementary substances and of radicals whose valence is not divisible by two without a remainder. Contrasted with artiad.
pectination: 1. The state of being pectinated; that which is pectinated. Sir T. Browne. 2. The act of combing; the combing of the head. 3. (Nat. Hist.) Comblike toothing.
pedestaled: Placed on, or supported by, a pedestal; figuratively, exalted. Hawthorne. Pedestaled haply in a palace court. Keats.
perigraph: A careless or inaccurate delineation of anything. Etym:
penwoman: A female writer; an authoress. Johnson.

peachblow: Of the delicate purplish pink color likened to that of peach blooms; -- applied esp. to a Chinese porcelain, small specimens of which bring great prices in the Western countries.
perpetually: In a perpetual manner; constantly; continually. The Bible and Common Prayer Book in the vulgar tongue, being perpetually read in churches, have proved a kind of standard for language. Swift.
pederero: A term formerly applied to a short piece of chambered ordnance. [Written also paterero and peterero.]
pentagon: A plane figure having five angles, and, consequently, five sides; any figure having five angles. Regular pentagon, a pentagon in which the angles are all equal, and the sides all equal.
pendent: 1. Supported from above; suspended; depending; pendulous; hanging; as, a pendent leaf. "The pendent world." Shak. Often their tresses, when shaken, with pendent icicles tinkle. Longfellow. 2. Jutting over; projecting; overhanging. "A vapor sometime like a . . . pendent rock." Shak.
permeability: The quality or state of being permeable. Magnetic permeability (Physics), the specific capacity of a body for magnetic induction, or its conducting power for lines of magnetic force. Sir W. Thomson.
pedometer: An instrument for including the number of steps in walking, and so ascertaining the distance passed over. It is usually in the form of a watch; an oscillating weight by the motion of the body causes the index to advance a certain distance at each step.
pentapody: A measure or series consisting of five feet.
perithecium: An organ in certain fungi and lichens, surrounding and enveloping the masses of fructification. Henslow.
persuasible: 1. Capable of being persuaded; persuadable. 2. Persuasive. (old) Bale. -- Per*sua"si*ble*ness, n. -- Per*sua"si*bly, adv.
perturbable: Liable to be perturbed or agitated; liable to be disturbed or disquieted.
periproct: The region surrounding the anus, particularly of echinoderms.
perceivable: Capable of being perceived; perceptible. -- Per*ceiv"a*bly, adv.
perspirative: Performing the act of perspiration; perspiratory.
pentosan: One of a class of substances (complex carbohydrates widely distributed in plants, as in fruits, gums, woods, hay, etc.) which yield pentoses on hydrolysis.
penk: A minnow. See Pink, n., 4. [Prov. Eng.] Walton.
peckish: Inclined to eat; hungry. [Colloq.] "When shall I feel peckish again" Beaconsfield.
pennant: (a) A small flag; a pennon. The narrow, or long, pennant (called also whip or coach whip) is a long, narrow piece of bunting, carried at the masthead of a government vessel in commission. pelotage: Packs or bales of Spanish wool.
petasus: The winged cap of Mercury; also, a broad-brimmed, low-crowned hat worn by Greeks and Romans.
pell: To pelt; to knock about. (old) Holland. | 1. A skin or hide; a pelt. 2. A roll of parchment; a parchment record. Clerk of the pells, formerly, an officer of the exchequer who entered accounts on certain parchment rolls, called pell rolls.
peract: To go through with; to perform. (old) Sylvester.
peplum: A peplos. Hence: An overskirt hanging like an ancient peplos; also, a short fitted skirt attached to a waist or coat.
pedipalpous: Pertaining to, or resembling, the pedipalps.
peaceable: Begin in or at peace; tranquil; quiet; free from, or not disposed to, war, disorder, or excitement; not quarrelsome. -- Peace"a*ble*ness, n. -- Peace"a*bly, adv. peagrit: A coarse pisolitic limestone. See Pisolite.
periscians: Those who live within a polar circle, whose shadows, during some summer days, will move entirely round, falling toward every point of the compass.
pencel: A small, narrow flag or streamer borne at the top of a lance; - - called also pennoncel. (old) Piers Plowman. Chaucer.
perimetry: The art of using the perimeter; measurement of the field of vision.
pergolo: A continuous colonnade or arcade; -- applied to the decorative groups of windows, as in Venetian palazzi.
pentavalent: Having a valence of five; -- said of certain atoms and radicals.
perfectional: Of or pertaining to perfection; characterized by perfection. Bp. Pearson.
pensileness: State or quality of being pensile; pendulousness.
percursory: Running over slightly or in haste; cursory.
pentelic: Of or pertaining to Mount Pentelicus, near Athens, famous for its fine white marble quarries; obtained from Mount Pentelicus; as, the Pentelic marble of which the Parthenon is built.

petrificate: To petrify. (old) Our hearts petrificated were. J. Hall (1646).

periosteum: The membrane of fibrous connective tissue which closely invests all bones except at the articular surfaces.
perisystole: The interval between the diastole and systole of the heart. It is perceptible only in the dying.
pent: Penned or shut up; confined; -- often with up. Here in the body pent. J. Montgomery. No pent-up Utica contracts your powers. J. M. Sewall.
pewter: 1. A hard, tough, but easily fusible, alloy, originally consisting of tin with a little lead, but afterwards modified by the addition of copper, antimony, or bismuth. 2. perceiver: One who perceives (in any of the senses of the verb). Milton.
petalody: The metamorphosis of various floral organs, usually stamens, into petals.
perturbed: Agitated; disturbed; troubled. Shak. -- Per*turb"ed*ly, adv.
perdifoil: A deciduous plant; -- opposed to Ant: evergreen. J. Barton.

penuchle: A game at cards, played with forty-eight cards, being all the cards above the eight spots in two packs.
peplis: A genus of plants including water purslane.
peorias: An Algonquin tribe of Indians who formerly inhabited a part of Illinois.
pentadactyle: 1. (Anat.) Having five digits to the hand or foot. 2. Having five appendages resembling fingers or toes.
petalous: Having petals; petaled; -- opposed to Ant: apetalous.
peridium: The envelope or coat of certain fungi, such as the puffballs and earthstars.
perrier: A short mortar used formerly for throwing stone shot. Hakluyt.
peise: A weight; a poise. (old) "To weigh pence with a peise." Piers Plowman. | To poise or weight. (old) Chaucer. Lest leaden slumber peise me down. Shak.
pellagrin: One who is afficted with pellagra. Chambers's Encyc.
perispore: The outer covering of a spore.
petaliform: Having the form of a petal; petaloid; petal-shaped.
pedrail: (a) A device intended to replace the wheel of a self-propelled vehicle for use on rough roads and to approximate to the smoothness in running of a wheel on a metal track. The tread consists of a number of rubber shod feet which are connected by ball-and-socket joints to the ends of sliding spokes.
permissible: That may be permitted; allowable; admissible. -- Per*mis"si*ble*ness, n. -- Per*mis"si*bly, adv.
petersham: A rough, knotted woolen cloth, used chiefly for men's overcoats; also, a coat of that material.
pearl: A fringe or border. (old) -- v. t. To fringe; to border. (old) See Purl. Pearl stitch. See Purl stitch, under Purl. | 1. (Zoöl.) penetrative: 1. Tending to penetrate; of a penetrating quality; piercing; as, the penetrative sun. His look became keen and penetrative. Hawthorne. 2. Having the power to affect or impress the mind or heart; impressive; as, penetrative shame. Shak. 3. Acute; discerning; sagacious; as, penetrative wisdom. "The penetrative eye." Wordsworth. Led on by skill of penetrative soul. Grainger.
penanglawyer: A kind of walking stick made from the stem of an East Asiatic palm (Licuala acutifida).
petaloideous: Having the whole or part of the perianth petaline. Petaloideous division, that division of endogenous plants in which the perianth is wholly or partly petaline, embracing the Liliaceæ, Orchidaceæ, Amaryllideæ, etc.
penitentiaryship: The office or condition of a penitentiary of the papal court. Wood.
petit: Small; little; insignificant; mean; -- Same as Petty. [Obs., except in legal language.] By what small, petit hints does the mind catch hold of and recover a vanishing notion. South. Petit constable, an inferior civil officer, subordinate to the high constable. -- Petit jury, a jury of twelve men, impaneled to try causes at the bar of a court;
pedant: 1. A schoolmaster; a pedagogue. (old) Dryden. A pedant that keeps a school i'th' church. Shak. 2. One who puts on an air of learning; one who makes a vain display of learning; a pretender to superior knowledge. Addison. A scholar, yet surely no pedant, was he. Goldsmith.
peter: A common baptismal name for a man. The name of one of the apostles, Peter boat, a fishing boat, sharp at both ends, originally of the Baltic Sea, but now common in certain English rivers. | To become exhausted; to run out; to fail; -- used generally with out; as, that mine has petered out. [Slang, U.S.]
permeable: Capable of being permeated, or passed through; yielding passage; passable; penetrable; -- used especially of substances which allow the passage of fluids; as, wood is permeable to oil; glass is permeable to light. I. Taylor.
perilous: 1. Full of, attended with, or involving, peril; dangerous; hazardous; as, a perilous undertaking. Infamous hills, and sandy, perilous wilds. Milton. 2. Daring; reckless; dangerous. (old) Latimer. For I am perilous with knife in hand. Chaucer. -- Per"il*ous*ly, adv. -- Per"il*ous*ness, n.
percussion: 1. The act of percussing, or striking one body against another; forcible collision, esp. such as gives a sound or report. Sir I. Newton. 2. Hence: The effect of violent collision; vibratory shock; impression of sound on the ear. The thunderlike percussion of thy sounds. Shak. 3.
penetrance: The quality or state of being penetrant; power of entering or piercing; penetrating power of quality; as, the penetrancy of subtile effluvia.
percipience: The faculty, act or power of perceiving; perception. Mrs. Browning.
perinephritis: Inflammation of the cellular tissue around the kidney. -- Per`i*ne*phrit"ic, a.
petalosticha: An order of Echini, including the irregular sea urchins, as the spatangoids. See Spatangoid.
peregrinity: 1. Foreignness; strangeness. (old) "Somewhat of a peregrinity in their dialect." Johnson. 2. Travel; wandering. Carlyle.
pectolite: A whitish mineral occurring in radiated or fibrous crystalline masses. It is a hydrous silicate of lime and soda.
personalty: 1. The state of being a person; personality. 2. (Law) Personal property, as distinguished from realty or real property.
peccavi: I have sinned; -- used colloquially to express confession or acknowledgment of an offense. Aubrey.
persecutor: One who persecutes, or harasses. Shak.
periodicalist: One who publishes, or writes for, a periodical.
pezizoid: Resembling a fungus of the genus Peziza; having a cuplike form.
perfidy: The act of violating faith or allegiance; violation of a promise or vow, or of trust reposed; faithlessness; teachery. The ambition and perfidy of tyrants. Macaulay. His perfidy to this sacred engagement. DeQuincey.
penniless: Destitute of money; impecunious; poor. -- Pen"ni*less*ness, n.
pedestrianism: The act, art, or practice of a pedestrian; walking or running; traveling or racing on foot.
persicot: A cordial made of the kernels of apricots, nectarines, etc., with refined spirit.
periphrase: The use of more words than are necessary to express the idea; a roundabout, or indirect, way of speaking; circumlocution. "To describe by enigmatic periphrases." De Quincey. | To express by periphrase or circumlocution.
persevere: To persist in any business or enterprise undertaken; to pursue steadily any project or course begun; to maintain a purpose in spite of counter influences, opposition, or discouragement; not to give or abandon what is undertaken. Thrice happy, if they know Their happiness, and persevere upright. Milton. Syn. -- To Persevere, Continue, Persist.
perish: To be destroyed; to pass away; to become nothing; to be lost; to die; hence, to wither; to waste away. I perish with hunger! Luke xv. 17. Grow up and perish, as the summer fly. Milton. The thoughts of a soul that perish in thinking. Locke.
peart: Active; lively; brisk; smart; -- often applied to convalescents; as, she is quite peart to-day. [O. Eng. & Colloq. U. S.] There was a tricksy girl, I wot, albeit clad in gray, As peart as bird, as straight as bolt, as fresh as flowers in May. Warner (1592).
pebblestone: A pebble; also, pebbles collectively. "Chains of pebblestone." Marlowe.
permute: 1. To interchange; to transfer reciprocally. 2. To exchange; to barter; to traffic. (old) Bought, trucked, permuted, or given. Hakluyt.
pertinacy: The quality or state of being pertinent; pertinence. (old)
peddle: 1. To travel about with wares for sale; to go from place to place, or from house to house, for the purpose of retailing goods; as, to peddle without a license. 2. To do a small business; | To sell from place to place; to retail by carrying around from customer to customer; to hawk; hence, to retail in very small quantities; as, to peddle vegetables or tinware.
perdix: A genus of birds including the common European partridge. Formerly the word was used in a much wider sense to include many allied genera.
ped: A basket; a hammer; a pannier. (old) Halliwell.
pernor: One who receives the profits, as of an estate.
peascod: The legume or pericarp, or the pod, of the pea.
perca: A genus of fishes, including the fresh-water perch.
petune: To spray (tobacco) with a liquid intended to produce flavor or aroma.
percarbureted: Combined with a relatively large amount of carbon.
periclitate: To endanger. (old) Periclitating, pardi! the whole family. Sterne.
penannular: Nearly annular; having nearly the form of a ring. "Penannular relics." D. Wilson.
pewfellow: 1. One who occupies the same pew with another. 2. An intimate associate; a companion. Shak.
pectosic: Of, pertaining to, resembling, or derived from, pectose; specifically, designating an acid supposed to constitute largely ordinary pectin or vegetable jelly.
peptonuria: The presence of peptone, or a peptonelike body, in the urine.
pedograph: An instrument carried by a pedestrian for automatically making a topographical record of the ground covered during a journey.
pentadelphous: Having the stamens arranged in five clusters, those of each cluster having their filaments more or less united, as the flowers of the linden.
perpendicular: 1. Exactly upright or vertical; pointing to the zenith; at right angles to the plane of the horizon; extending in a right line from any point toward the center of the earth. 2. | 1. perspicuity: 1. The quality or state of being transparent or translucent. (old) Sir T. Browne. 2. The quality of being perspicuous to the understanding; clearness of expression or thought. 3. Sagacity; perspicacity. Syn. -- Clearness; perspicuousness; plainness; distinctness; lucidity; transparency. See Clearness.
penguin: 1. (Zoöl.) Any bird of the order Impennes, or Ptilopteri. They are covered with short, thick feathers, almost scalelike on the wings, which are without true quills. They are unable to fly, but use their wings to aid in diving, in which they are very expert. See King penguin, under Jackass. Note: Penguins are found in the south temperate and antarctic regions.
pennaceous: Like or pertaining to a normal feather.
peony: A plant, and its flower, of the ranunculaceous genus Pæonia. Of the four or five species, one is a shrub; the rest are perennial herbs with showy flowers, often double in cultivation. [Written also pæony, and piony.]
pedate: Palmate, with the lateral lobes cleft into two or more segments; -- said of a leaf. -- Ped"ate*ly, adv.
perpendicle: Something hanging straight down; a plumb line. (old)
pelfry: Pelf; also, figuratively, rubbish; trash. (old) Cranmer.
perilla: A genus of labiate herbs, of which one species (Perilla ocimoides, or P. Nankinensis) is often cultivated for its purple or variegated foliage.
pectic: Of or pertaining to pectin; specifically, designating an acid obtained from ordinary vegetable jelly (pectin) as an amorphous substance, tough and horny when dry, but gelatinous when moist.
pectous: Of, pertaining to, or consisting of, pectose.
pedimental: Of or pertaining to a pediment.
persulphide: A sulphide containing more sulphur than some other compound of the same elements; as, iron pyrites is a persulphide; -- formerly called persulphuret.
pernoctation: The act or state of passing the whole night; a remaining all night. "Pernoctation in prayer." Jer. Taylor.
pericellular: Surrounding a cell; as, the pericellular lymph spaces surrounding ganglion cells.
permissive: 1. Permitting; granting leave or liberty. "By his permissive will." Milton. 2. Permitted; tolerated; suffered. Milton.
pedantical: Of or pertaining to a pedant; characteristic of, or resembling, a pedant; ostentatious of learning; as, a pedantic writer; a pedantic description; a pedantical affectation. "Figures pedantical." Shak.
pedanty: An assembly or clique of pedants. (old) Milton.
peritropal: 1. Rotatory; circuitous. 2. Having the axis of the seed perpendicular to the axis of the pericarp to which it is attached.
pedestrious: Going on foot; not winged. (old) "Pedestrious animals." Sir T. Browne.
pediculati: An order of fishes including the anglers. See Illust. of Angler and Batfish.
perspicience: The act of looking sharply. (old) Bailey.
perigastric: Surrounding the stomach; -- applied to the body cavity of Bryozoa and various other Invertebrata.
pentafid: Divided or cleft into five parts.
peribranchial: Surrounding the branchiæ; as, a peribranchial cavity. | Around the bronchi or bronchial tubes; as, the peribronchial lymphatics.
periwig: A headdress of false hair, usually covering the whole head, and representing the natural hair; a wig. Shak. | To dress with a periwig, or with false hair. Swift.
pertusion: The act of punching or piercing with a pointed instrument; as, pertusion of a vein. Arbuthnot. 2. A punched hole; a perforation. Bacon.
pentateuchal: Of or pertaining to the Pentateuch.
petrescent: Petrifying; converting into stone; as, petrescent water. Boyle.
pectinibranch: One of the Pectinibranchiata. Also used adjectively.
pedestrianize: To practice walking; to travel on foot.
periplast: Same as Periblast. -- Per`i*plas"tic, a. Huxley.
peristeromorphous: Like or pertaining to the pigeons or Columbæ.
peziza: A genus of fungi embracing a great number of species, some of which are remarkable for their regular cuplike form and deep colors.
petard: A case containing powder to be exploded, esp. a conical or cylindrical case of metal filled with powder and attached to a plank, to be exploded against and break down gates, barricades, drawbridges, etc. It has been superseded.
perdue: 1. Lost to view; in concealment or ambush; close. He should lie perdue who is to walk the round. Fuller. 2. Accustomed to, or employed in, desperate enterprises; hence, reckless; hopeless. "A perdue captain." Beau. & Fl.
perivascular: Around the blood vessels; as, perivascular lymphatics.
peanutbutter: A paste made by mixing ground fresh roasted peanuts with a small quantity of water or oil, and used chiefly as a relish on sandwiches, etc.
periapt: A charm worn as a protection against disease or mischief; an amulet. Coleridge. Now help, ye charming spells and periapts. Shak.
persuasive: Tending to persuade; having the power of persuading; as, persuasive eloquence. "Persuasive words." Milton. | That which persuades; an inducement; an incitement; an exhortation. -- Per*sua"sive*ly, adv. -- Per*sua"sive*ness, n.
perpetrator: One who perpetrates; esp., one who commits an offense or crime.
peptotoxine: A toxic alkaloid found occasionally associated with the peptones formed from fibrin by pepsinhydrochloric acid.
perturb: 1. To disturb; to agitate; to vex; to trouble; to disquiet. Ye that . . . perturb so my feast with crying. Chaucer. 2. To disorder; to confuse. Sir T. Browne.
penetration: 1. The act or process of penetrating, piercing, or entering; also, the act of mentally penetrating into, or comprehending, anything difficult. Acuteness; insight; sharp discoverment; sagacity;
petromastoid: Of or pertaining to the petrous and mastoid parts of the temporal bone, periotic.
perinuclear: Of or pertaining to a nucleus; situated around a nucleus; as, the perinuclear protoplasm.
pendulosity: The state or quality of being pendulous. Sir T. Browne.
peptonize: To convert into peptone; to digest or dissolve by means of a proteolytic ferment; as, peptonized food.
pentagynous: Of or pertaining to plants of the order Pentagyna; having five styles.
pedunculated: Having a peduncle; growing on a peduncle; as, a pedunculate flower; a pedunculate eye, as in a lobster.
peltiereffect: The production or absorption of heat at the junction of two metals on the passage of a current. A cross formed of two strips of different metals, to illustrate the Peltier effect.
peseta: A Spanish silver coin, and money of account, equal to about nineteen cents, and divided into 100 centesimos.
pedatifid: Cleft in a pedate manner, but having the lobes distinctly connected at the base; -- said of a leaf.
perpetual: Neverceasing; continuing forever or for an unlimited time; unfailing; everlasting; continuous. Unto the kingdom of perpetual night. Shak. Perpetual feast of nectared sweets. Milton. pehlevi: An ancient Persian dialect in which words were partly represented by their Semitic equivalents. It was in use from the 3d century (and perhaps earlier) to the middle of the 7th century, and later in religious writings. [Written also Pahlavi.]
perigean: Pertaining to the perigee. Perigean tides, those spring tides which occur soon after the moon passes her perigee.
peck: 1. The fourth part of a bushel; a dry measure of eight quarts; as, a peck of wheat. "A peck of provender." Shak. 2. A great deal; a large or excessive quantity. pettychaps: Any one of several species of small European singing birds of the subfamily Sylviinæ, as the willow warbler, the chiff-chaff, and the golden warbler (Sylvia hortensis).
pennon: A pennant; a flag or streamer. Longfellow.
peltated: Shield-shaped; scutiform; (Bot.) having the stem or support attached to the lower surface, instead of at the base or margin; -- said of a leaf or other organ. -- Pel"tate*ly, adv.
pedantism: The office, disposition, or act of a pedant; pedantry. (old)
petitionee: A person cited to answer, or defend against, a petition.
periodical: 1. Of or pertaining to a period or periods, or to division by periods. The periodicaltimes of all the satellites. Sir J. Herschel. 2. Performed in a period, or regular revolution; | A magazine or other publication which appears at stated or regular intervals.
perquisited: Supplied with perquisites. (old) "Perquisited varlets frequent stand." Savage.
perry: A fermented liquor made from pears; pear cider. Mortimer. | A suddent squall. See Pirry. (old)
peal: A small salmon; a grilse; a sewin. [Prov. Eng.] | 1. A loud sound, or a succession of loud sounds, as of bells, thunder, cannon, shouts, of a multitude, etc. "A fair peal of artillery." Hayward. Whether those peals of praise be his or no. Shak.
pellucid: Transparent; clear; limpid; translucent; not opaque. "Pellucid crystal." Dr. H. More. "Pellucid streams." Wordsworth.
peristeria: A genus of orchidaceous plants. See Dove plant.
perrie: Precious stones; jewels. (old) [Written also perre, perrye, etc.] Chaucer.
pear: The fleshy pome, or fruit, of a rosaceous tree (Pyrus communis), cultivated in many varieties in temperate climates; also, the tree which bears this fruit. See Pear family, below. Pear blight.
perthite: A kind of feldspar consisting of a laminated intertexture of albite and orthoclase, usually of different colors. -- Per*thit"ic, a.
penultimate: Last but one; as, the penultimate syllable, the last syllable but one of a word.
pectinal: Of or pertaining to a comb; resembling a comb. | A fish whose bone Sir T. Browne.
peephole: A hole, or crevice, through which one may peep without being discovered.
peach: To accuse of crime; to inform against. (old) Foxe. | To turn informer; to betray one's accomplice. [Obs. or Colloq.] If I be ta'en, I'll peach for this. Shak.
pedo: Combining forms from L. pes, pedis, foot, as pedipalp, pedireme, pedometer.
pervade: 1. To pass or flow through, as an aperture, pore, or interstice; to permeate. That labyrinth is easily pervaded. Blackstone. 2. peperine: A volcanic rock, formed by the cementing together of sand, scoria, cinders, etc.
pedestrial: Of or pertaining to the feet; employing the foot or feet.
peregrinate: To travel from place to place, or from one country to another; hence, to sojourn in foreign countries. | Having traveled; foreign. (old) Shak.
petalite: A rare mineral, occurring crystallized and in cleavable masses, usually white, or nearly so, in color. It is a silicate of aluminia and lithia.
pentacid: Capable of neutralizing, or combining with, five molecules of a monobasic acid; having five hydrogen atoms capable of substitution by acid residues; -- said of certain complex bases.
perhaps: By chance; peradventure; perchance; it may be. And pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee. Acts viii. 22.
perlitic: Relating to or resembling perlite, or pearlstone; as, the perlitic structure of certain rocks. See Pearlite.
permeate: 1. To pass through the pores or interstices of; to penetrate and pass through without causing rupture or displacement; -- applied especially to fluids which pass through substances of loose texture; as, water permeates sand. Woodward. 2. To enter and spread through; to pervade. God was conceived to be diffused throughout the whole world, to permeate and pervade all things.
pelerine: A woman's cape; especially, a fur cape that is longer in front than behind. PELE'S HAIR Pe"le's hair. [After a Hawaiian goddess associated with the crater Kilauea.] Glass threads or fibers formed by the wind from bits blown from frothy lava or from the tips of lava jets or from bits of liquid lava thrown into the air. It often collects in thick masses resembling tow.
